title: Cohort shepherding & observability play notes
body:
Overview:
Quick notes about running tiny-cohort experiments with strong observability coupling. Intended as a lightweight steward handbook: how to watch, when to escalate, how to steer exposures when cost or latency budgets start drifting. Mostly raw thinking and a checklist for on-call/steward rotations.

Context:
- Use case: staged rollout of reranker+response-rerank step that can increase tail latency. We need a cross-team plan (product, infra, SRE, data) to shepherd cohorts while preserving cost and latency SLOs.
- Constraints: 2% global exposure initially, must enforce 99th pct latency < 420ms and incremental cost < 7% for first week.

Goals for steward ops:
- Detect behavioral drift (quality), latency regressions, cost spikes early.
- Provide a clear decision ladder (observe -> throttle -> quarantine -> rollback) with owner and SLAs.
- Keep manual interventions simple and reversible.

Signal set (primary -> immediate action):
1) 99p latency (user-facing) rising > +60ms over baseline for 5m -> throttle cohort by 50%
2) Error rate increase +0.2% absolute over baseline for 3m -> pause new sessions to cohort and notify oncall
3) Token-cost-per-request up > +10% sustained 30m -> trigger cost-quarantine review with finance rep
4) Quality regression on golden prompts (evaluation harness): drop in top-1 accuracy > 3% -> stop exposure and open regression ticket

Derived metrics to surface on dashboard (minimum):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 overall and per-cohort, p99 delta vs baseline
- Cost: tokens/request, GPU minutes/hour attributable to cohort routes
- Quality: golden-set pass rate, novelty/adversarial flags, user-reported safety hits
- Traffic shape: request size distribution, prefix reuse rate (cache hit), batching efficiency
- Fallbacks: percent of requests routed to fallback path and reason codes

Dashboard placement / owners:
- SRE dashboard (real-time): latency, error rate, fallback percent; owner: Lina Chen
- Cost dashboard (hourly): cost delta and allocation; owner: Marcus Green
- Product evaluation (nightly): golden-set accuracy + example traces; owner: Priya Shah

Steward rotation & quick roles:
- Steward (hour): primary contact for small adjustments — can throttle via console slider (0.5x increments).
- Incident lead (escalation): owns decision to quarantine/rollback.
- Infra liaison: fast path to scale more dedicated capacity or switch routing to cheaper variant.
- Communications owner: prepares the short incident blurb for stakeholders and CS.

Quick runbook (for oncall/steward):
- Step 0: look up cohort id and current exposure percentage in console. Confirm linked PR/commit.
- Step 1: check SRE dashboard p99 and error rate. If threshold breached, throttle cohort to half exposure and re-evaluate in 5m.
- Step 2: check fallback percent. If >5% after throttling, open JIRA with tag #canary-fallback and inform infra.
- Step 3: run golden-set eval locally (run-eval --cohort <id>) and inspect top 10 failing prompts. If semantic regression observed, rollback.
- Step 4: on rollback: set cohort exposure 0%, trigger rollback API (rollback-to-stable --cohort <id>), notify Product and SRE, schedule postmortem.

Soft-automation ideas (short list):
- Auto-throttle rule: if p99 delta > 80ms for 3m AND fallback% > 2% => auto-throttle 60% (experiment to reduce human latency)
- Canary re-balance: run small synthetic traffic to failing slices to decide whether regressions are cohort-specific or global
- Cost budget alarm: tie to billing pipeline to create automatic small-scale alerts (not full incident)

Experiment design notes (for A/B runs involving cohorts):
- Hypothesis format: "Changing reranker X will increase click-through by Y% while keeping p99 latency within Z ms and cost delta < C%"
- Minimal data required before expansion: 48h of stable signal and n>=2000 requests for slice to avoid noisy stats
- Randomization: seed-based deterministic assignment per-user to avoid cross-cohort contamination across multi-request sessions
- Cross-team pre-checks: security review, privacy checklist, and QA sign-off on golden-set results

Communication patterns / templates:
- Slack snapshot (when throttled): short title + 1-line cause + actions taken + next check time + ticket link. Example: "[CANARY] cohort-17 throttle -> p99 +82ms; throttled to 25% at 11:12; re-check 11:17; JIRA RINF-842 opened"
- Stakeholder blurb (if quarantine): 3 bullets: what happened, impact, next steps (owner/times)

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Should we allow auto-throttle logic to perform multi-step backoffs (25% -> 0) without human approval? risk: false positives in noisy windows.
- Exact golden-set size and refresh cadence for nightly evaluation (current note: 120 prompts, need to expand to cover more edge cases).
- Mapping of user-visible features to cohort ids in console is messy; propose a small metadata schema change (add product_name, feature_tag to cohort metadata).
- Need a test harness for cost attribution per-cohort when requests route through shared batching layer.

Simulation checklist (pre-run synthetic rehearsals):
- Create synthetic population of 10k users with 2% cohort assignment.
- Simulate request distribution skewed to top 10% heavy users to validate tail behavior.
- Inject 3 failure modes: slow kernel (adds 120ms per token), cache cold start, and a model-version-quality drop.
- Run 3 replicas of each scenario and collect p99, fallback percent, and cost delta.

Notes to self (handy commands and tips):
- console: list-cohorts --filter product:inbox -> get IDs and exposure
- infra-tool: re-route --cohort <id> --variant cheap-quantized (useful for rapid cost experiments)
- eval harness: run-eval --cohort <id> --golden-set nightly/golden-v2

Examples of quick decisions and rationale (past learnings):
- Learned: throttling early fixed many tail latency spikes because the problem was KV cache pressure not model quality. So first action is throttle, not rollback.
- Learned: small cost increases (<=5%) are tolerable if quality improves more than 6% on golden-set. Make decision rules explicit.

Appendix (links):
- Quick playbook draft for console controls: CONF-2319
- Incident ticket template: template/incident-runbook-lite

End notes:
- Keep this doc short, iterate into a proper runbook once we validate the auto-throttle rules in the simulator.
- Next steps: schedule a 1.5h run with SRE + infra + product to rehearse throttles and rollback (owners: Priya/Lina).
